overview: This tiny display packs real graphics capability — arbitrary pixels, custom fonts, simple animations, small bitmaps — into a screen the size of a fingernail, using OLED pixels that emit their own light rather than needing a backlight. That makes contrast excellent and power draw proportional to how many pixels are actually lit (a mostly-black screen sips very little power), a genuine advantage over an LCD's fixed backlight draw. It talks over I2C (some variants also support SPI) and is driven by the widely-supported SSD1306 controller chip, which nearly every graphics library (Adafruit_SSD1306, u8g2) has first-class support for.
simpleSummary: A tiny, crisp screen that can show real graphics, text, and simple animations.

specifications.displayType: Monochrome OLED (no backlight needed, self-emitting pixels)

pinMap.currentLimit: ~20 mA typical, varies with lit pixel count

pinMap.gotcha: Multiple I2C devices sharing a bus with this display must all use different addresses — the SSD1306 defaults to 0x3C, occasionally 0x3D.

useCases.title: Compact status/graphics display
